data.long_meaning: Lord Shiva, the young one. The name Shivakumar carries the meaning “Shiva + Young Lord” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Tamil, Telugu. Parents who choose Shivakumar usually hope their child will grow to embody shiva + young lord and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the supreme god Shiva and the young and energetic phase of life
data.etymology: Shivakumar belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Shiva + Young Lord.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shivakumar total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Shivakumar" is a popular name among Hindus, meaning 'associated with Lord Shiva'. Lord Shiva is one of the primary deities in Hinduism and is known as the god of destruction and transformation. He is also considered as the supreme God who destroys all our impurities and negativities. The name Shivakumar reflects this deep reverence and devotion towards Lord Shiva. It is a common name that is passed down through generations in many Hindu families.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name "Shivakumar" lies in the deep connection it represents between the individual and Lord Shiva. The 'Shiva' part represents the divine enlightenment that the individual aspires towards, while the 'Kumar' part signifies the young and enthusiastic nature of the individual's spiritual journey. It is believed that using this name invokes Lord Shiva's blessings and guidance, enabling the individual to overcome the challenges of life and achieve spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Shivakumar is a name that embodies the divine presence of Lord Shiva and the nurturing energy of Lord Kumar (Lord Kartikeya or Subramanya). It signifies the union of the destructive and creative forces in the universe, symbolizing transformation and regeneration.

historical_references.reference: Shivakumar was a famous temple priest in the temple town of Tiruvannamalai, Tamil Nadu, India. He is believed to have lived during the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

Shivakumar Swami, also known as Swami Sivapadananda, was a renowned Hindu scholar and spiritual leader. He is believed to have lived during the 19th and mid-20th centuries and is known for his contributions to the Advaita Vedanta philosophy.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Shivakumar' holds deep spiritual significance in Hindu culture. In modern times, this name is seen on various platforms such as LinkedIn, Twitter, and Instagram. On LinkedIn, individuals with this name might be professionals in various fields like technology, engineering, or finance. On Twitter, Shivakumars might be engaging in spiritual discourses and debates, sharing their perspectives and knowledge. Lastly, on Instagram, they might be sharing images and quotes related to spirituality, technology, or philanthropy, reflecting the balanced nature of the name.
